brief: The Market Ear (citing BTIG, GS, JPM and UBS) argues the equity bounce faces a hard test. SPX snapped from oversold to major resistance at 7350-7400 (the 200-day average) in one session. BTIG's history: 42 prior NDX 6%+ rallies while below the 200-day average since 1985 produced a median 30-day return of -5.35% (up only 39% of the time); the 12 prior one-day -5%/+5% reversals saw just two positive next days, a -4.9% average 5-day return and a 16.4% average 30-day drawdown, though the average 30-day draw-up was near 10%, concentrated after day 15. S&P E-mini open interest rose $36.6bn as the index fell 5.9% (Nov 17-20) but fell only $7.9bn in Monday's squeeze, implying fresh longs or surviving shorts, so TME sees fuel left in the squeeze. Bitcoin gave back its Jensen-driven gains. JPMorgan's Adler says removing Jensen uncertainty helps NVDA, but government intervention in governance risks equity multiples longer-term; he still sees room to rally. UBS stays neutral, rotating out of megacap AI concentration into equal-weight, Europe, industrials and healthcare as the AI debate shifts from spending scale to funding quality and returns. VIX sits near 30, close to March's panic peak, despite SPX futures barely down.
